methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $2.3B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 9 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Divergent operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at Series E with a last post-money valuation of $2.3B and $600M+ in cumulative funding. The applicable peer universe comprises nine private companies in the same sector and valuation tier, supplemented by one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ). Representative peers include Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Locus Robotics ($2.0B, Series F), and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), with the peer cohort spanning $1.0B to $2.0B.

Two valuation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression applies a 1.4x multiplier to the $2.3B base, yielding $3.2B, reflecting typical capital infusion and value creation across a Series E-to-next-stage transition. Peer-median benchmarking across nine robotics companies produces $1.6B, with a range floor of $1.0B and ceiling of $2.0B, though this method's result sits materially below the target's last raise, likely reflecting a heterogeneous peer set spanning earlier stages.

Triangulation across both methods supports a range of $1.4B (low) to $3.7B (high), with a median of $2.4B. The current valuation of $2.3B aligns closely with this midpoint. Key uncertainties include peer-set heterogeneity—the nine comparables span Series B through Series F stages—and the appropriate stage-progression multiple in a robotics sector characterized by prolonged capital needs and commercialization timelines. Revenue visibility and path to profitability would meaningfully narrow this range.
